reason: The text demonstrates that non-leaders—the Israelite people (עם)—exercise significant agency throughout. They collectively accept the covenant ('all the people answered with one voice'), actively assemble to make demands of Aaron, voluntarily remove and provide their gold earrings, participate in religious rituals, and make the crucial decision to worship the golden calf. These are independent actions, not mere passive compliance with leader directives. The people are portrayed as agents with decision-making capacity, not as entirely dependent on leaders for agency.
